video_title: Microservices: Why split a working monolith?
core_insight: Microservices solve organizational and scaling coupling, not just technical scaling. The hard part is boundaries, data ownership and eventual consistency.

scenes.voice: A monolith works great, until it doesn't. Why do teams split it into microservices?
scenes.visual: Simple monolith box with Client -> Monolith -> DB. Then traffic spike icon on Checkout.

scenes.voice: The real problem isn't code size. It's uneven scale, team bottlenecks, and change coupling. Checkout is hot at Black Friday, catalog isn't. You end up scaling everything.
scenes.visual: Monolith box with Checkout hot, Catalog cold, and scale arrows up on whole box.

scenes.voice: Obvious fix? Split by feature. But the first reasonable approach is a modular monolith: clear module boundaries, one deployable. You get organization without operational explosion.
scenes.visual: Monolith with internal modules Order, Payment, Inventory separated by lines.

scenes.voice: Constraint appears. Fifty engineers on one repo means merge conflicts and risky deploys. A pricing tweak forces testing billing, search and UI together. You need independent deploy velocity.
scenes.visual: Multiple engineers icons converging on one repo, red deploy risk.

scenes.voice: That's when microservices make sense. Small independently deployable services, each owning a business capability and its own data. Network boundaries replace in-process calls.
scenes.visual: Diagram of Client -> API Gateway -> Order Service with orders DB, Payment Service with payments DB, Inventory Service with inventory DB.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR C[Client] --> GW[API Gateway] GW --> S1[Order Service
orders DB] GW --> S2[Payment Service
payments DB] GW --> S3[Inventory Service
inventory DB] S1 <--> S2 S1 <--> S3

scenes.voice: Trade-off? You gain team autonomy and heterogeneous scale. You pay with distributed complexity: latency, timeouts, partial failure, and no ACID across services. Consistency becomes eventual, via sagas and events.
scenes.visual: Scale icons: Order 100 pods, Catalog 10 pods. Then warning icons for network, retries, eventual consistency.

scenes.voice: Mental model: services map to teams. Conway's Law made explicit. The boundary is the hard part. Don't split for tech fashion. Split when coupling cost is measurable.
scenes.visual: Teams icons mapping 1:1 to services, with boundary lines emphasized.

scenes.voice: Start modular, split when you must. Microservices solve organizational coupling, not just scaling.
scenes.visual: Monolith -> Modular Monolith -> Microservices progression with decision gate.

mental_model: Think Problem → Constraints → Options → Trade-offs → Decision. Microservices are a response to organizational and scaling coupling. The boundary defines data ownership and consistency model. Map services to teams, and only split when the cost of coupling is measurable.
final_takeaway: Microservices buy independent deploy velocity and bounded scale at the cost of distributed complexity. Start modular, split on measurable coupling.
